solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Effect backfiring in art gallery thus far

indicators.note: in says the reversed piece sits inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery

indicators.note: something backfiring goes the wrong way, so the word for effect is read backwards

parts.note: to effect something is to do it

explanation.surface: A gallery reports that an effect has misfired in its exhibition so far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Effect' is a verb here: to effect something is to do it. The Tate is the well-known London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning up until the present moment, the same as thus far.

clue.text: The aforementioned thing above church, covering for roof

indicators.note: in a down clue, above places the first piece on top of the second

parts.note: that refers back to a thing already mentioned

explanation.surface: Something already mentioned sits above a church, serving as its roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is straw or reeds laid as a roof covering on traditional cottages.

clue.text: Cold bum sanitised with soap

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so the letters that follow are put into a poor, jumbled order

explanation.surface: A rear end has been cleaned with soap, a mildly comic bathroom scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like the noun, but here it is the slang adjective meaning bad, signalling the anagram of SANITISED and SOAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cold in manner is unemotional and detached, which is what this word describes.

clue.text: Inuit as translated in African country

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Inuit's words are being translated in an African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a north African nation on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Author in dreadful strop penning introduction to Ulysses

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the anagrammed letters hold the next piece inside
dreadful suggests something badly made, so the word strop is rearranged
the introduction to a word is its first letter, here of Ulysses

explanation.surface: An author in a foul mood is writing the opening of Ulysses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges STROP to PROST, and 'penning' puts U, the first letter of Ulysses, inside it. A strop is a British word for a sulky tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Proust was the French novelist who wrote In Search of Lost Time.

clue.text: Perch set up in fact, so ordinary

indicators.note: set up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words fact, so ordinary

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A perch has been put in place, which is a fact and a quite ordinary one.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a place where a bird settles to rest, the same as a perch.

clue.text: Upper-class Albion fan he's turned out

indicators.note: turned means changed in form, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A posh supporter of Albion, a football club, has been turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the definition, meaning no longer in fashion, not part of the anagram signal. West Bromwich Albion and Brighton are English football clubs called Albion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out is no longer in style, the opposite of in, so it is unfashionable.

clue.text: Seat launched, did you say?

indicators.note: did you say asks about how a word is spoken, signalling a soundalike

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a seat was just launched across the room.
explanation.definitionFit: A throne is the ceremonial chair of a monarch, a grand kind of seat.

clue.text: Guns and other weaponry, eleven in London

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a store of weapons
second meaning: the London football club, eleven being a team

explanation.walkthrough: 'eleven' is a football team of eleven players; Arsenal is a north London football club, nicknamed the Gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a stockpile of weapons, and the name of a London football side.

clue.text: Metal outside in that place struck with force

indicators.note: outside says the metal's letters go round the other piece

explanation.surface: Metal outside in some spot was hit hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Leathered is British slang for beaten hard, from a thrashing with a leather strap.
explanation.definitionFit: To leather someone is slang for to thrash or hit them hard, as with a leather strap.

clue.text: Price one's willing to pay rotten, sovereign

parts.note: food that has gone off is rotten
ER is the royal cipher of the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A rotten sovereign coin fetches whatever price a buyer will give.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is also an old British gold coin, which steers the surface toward money.
explanation.definitionFit: An offer is the amount a buyer proposes to pay for something.

clue.text: Girl beyond cruel, originally kind

indicators.note: beyond places the girl after the letter from cruel
originally points to the start of the word cruel, its first letter

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl has gone past cruelty and was at heart kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kind' reads as an adjective in the surface, but it is the noun meaning sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A class is a category or sort, which is what kind means as a noun.

clue.text: Smith trashed Sinatra

indicators.note: trashed means wrecked, so the singer's name is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Smith has panned Frank Sinatra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smith' looks like a surname but is a metalworker, a skilled craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith is a craftsperson who works metal, an example of a skilled manual worker.

clue.text: The pig sat twirling food in long strands

indicators.note: twirling means spinning round, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A pig sat twirling its food, which came in long strands.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is pasta in long thin strings, often twirled round a fork.

clue.text: Boat off, head of consolidating company leaves

indicators.note: off means faulty or not right, so the word boat is rearranged
the head of a word is its first letter, here of consolidating

explanation.surface: A boat departs as the boss of a merging firm quits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb meaning departs, but it is the noun: dried leaves for smoking. 'off' turns BOAT into TOBA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco is the dried leaf of a plant, smoked or chewed.

clue.text: Fool around like ingenues initially, in semi-darkness

indicators.note: around says the fool's letters are wrapped about the next piece
initially takes the first letter of each of the words like and ingenues

explanation.surface: Innocent young women fool about in the dim light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reads as fooling around in the surface, but it is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilit describes the dim light of dusk, halfway between day and night.

clue.text: Cricketer's hat?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the player who delivers the ball in cricket
second meaning: a hard round felt hat, the derby

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that the hat belongs to the cricketer, but the clue is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bowler delivers the ball; a bowler is also a rounded felt hat.

clue.text: Story of wife and skipper

parts.note: one who skips is a hopper

explanation.surface: A tale about a man's wife and the captain of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skipper' suggests a captain, but here it is literally one who skips.
explanation.definitionFit: A whopper is a huge lie, and a story can mean a falsehood.

clue.text: Petition some people admired

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A petition that a number of people looked up to.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to make an earnest appeal, as a petition does.

clue.text: Refuse place: leave house

parts.note: a bin is where refuse goes

explanation.surface: Someone is told the rubbish place is here, then to leave the house.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the numbers game is also called house, after the call of a full house.
explanation.definitionFit: House, or housey-housey, is an old British name for the game of bingo.

clue.text: Rent since collected by general

indicators.note: collected by says the word for since is gathered inside the general

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general
as can mean since, as in as it rained

explanation.surface: Rent has been gathered by a general officer since some time ago.
explanation.definitionFit: To lease something is to rent it, paying for its use over a term.

clue.text: Measure of noise coming from celeb I'd beaten up

indicators.note: beaten up means battered out of shape, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A celebrity complains of a racket after being assaulted.
explanation.definitionFit: The decibel is the unit used to measure loudness of sound.

clue.text: In den, try cooking

indicators.note: cooking means mixing and preparing, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to have a go at cooking in your den.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition but is the definition: in fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is in is currently fashionable, which is trendy.

clue.text: Show-off regrets work that's been rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so these letters are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A show-off regrets a piece of work that was turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: A poseur is someone who puts on airs to impress, a show-off.
